mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level is inversely related to equity valuation multiples; a lower rate directly reduces the discount rate for future cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 5-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL reading exceeding 3.0% indicates accelerating inflation, which typically triggers a monetary tightening cycle and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, or Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through compressed equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), the Federal Reserve maintains accommodative monetary policy to stimulate the economy, compressing discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5%, or Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) reading exceeding 1000 thousand units indicates robust consumer demand, which typically leads to stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when HOUST > 1000, or Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly nonfarm payroll growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 200 thousand units signals a tightening labor market, which typically triggers inflation concerns and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when PAYEMS > 200, or Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly retail sales (RSAFS) reading exceeding 380 billion dollars indicates robust consumer spending, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when RSAFS > 380, or Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) reading below 110.0 signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically reduces corporate profits and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when INDPRO < 110.0, or Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
